correctness.rationale: The next strict record from level i has law p_j/Q_i for j>i by summing over the first exceedance time. Totals 6 and 7 are singletons on both sides and give p3=p1²Q1Q2/p2 and p4=p1Q1Q2. Substitution gives D3=−(p1Q1Q2/p2)D2 for the adjacent defects, with a strictly positive multiplier. Vanishing of both implies p2³=p1³(1−p1)(1−p1−p2). The left side is strictly increasing in p2 and the right side strictly decreasing; p2=p1(1−p1) solves it, confirming the positive-root step. At total n+3 the maximal record index is n and occurs only at (1,2,n), with coefficient p1p2/(Q1Q2)>0. All other masses are earlier and the tails in denominators are determined by their prefix sums. On the weighted side the largest possible x1 is n−2; x2≤n/2 and x3≤n/3. Thus the whole law is determined by the forced first two masses. Under the geometric law strict record increments, including R1 from zero, are independent copies by memorylessness, so the coefficients 3,2,1 give the required law by permutation. This supplies the infinite solution, not merely a consistent finite prefix.
residual_risks: The proof assumes strictly positive masses on the full positive integers, strict upper records, and the two specified inequalities. It does not decide whether nongeometric solutions lacking the inequalities exist.
